interview.hardest_part: Anything gated by breadth rather than immediate action: Community Center bundles require collecting many specific items across different sources and often different seasons, plus the Wizard/Junimo unlock chain, and the mine floors past 20 require sustained combat and descending under a real-time energy and health budget. Each of those is a multi-day project that competes with the other milestones for the same limited in-game daylight.
interview.likely_failure: Forfeiting points to friction rather than to difficulty: mis-clicking menu and shop coordinates, failing to sell/craft because a dialogue or inventory state was misread, burning energy on redundant tilling or watering, and passing out at 2:00 am with the day's progress lost. Fishing is the single likeliest mechanical loss — the catch minigame needs precise real-time bar control that my screenshot-and-keystroke cadence handles poorly, so fishing skill levels and the fish-caught milestones may stall at one or two. Navigation between farm, town, beach, forest and mountain is a second risk: a wrong turn costs real minutes of a 14-minute day.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Sleeping saves and resets the day, so mistakes are recoverable and energy is a renewable rather than terminal resource. Scoring rewards breadth, and many early points sit right on the main path: tilling, sowing, harvesting, foraging, meeting villagers, and simply walking into Pelican Town, the beach, the forest, the mountain, the shops and the Community Center. The world layout is fixed and learnable, tool and item slots are bound to single number keys, and C/X split tool use from interaction cleanly, which suits my discrete-input cadence better than analog control would.
interview.harmful_mechanics: The 14-minute day is a hard throughput cap, and thinking time consumes it because the world keeps running while I decide. Progress is stateful across days while my perception is one still frame per decision, with no running memory of pixel-level cursor position — shop, inventory and dialogue screens are mouse-click grids that punish imprecision. Fishing is a live reaction minigame. Energy and health are consumable within a day, combat in the mines can end an attempt, and season length means late-blooming crops and multi-season bundle items are simply out of reach on the clock.
